instructions: Pat the 1.25 lbs of cod dry with paper towels and cut it into 8 pieces. Transfer them into a large bowl.

Grate the garlic and the 2 tsp of ginger into a small bowl. Cut the lemon in half and squeeze one half in, about 2 tbsp. Add 1/2 tsp of the salt, the turmeric, garam masala, coriander and 1/2 tsp of the chili powder, and stir to a paste. Rub the paste into the fish and let it sit for 8 minutes.

Meanwhile, finely chop the leaves from 1 sprig of the curry leaves. In a shallow dish, mix the rice flour, chickpea flour, the remaining 1/4 tsp of salt, the remaining 1/2 tsp of chili powder and the chopped curry leaves. Slice the onion into thin rings and cut the other lemon half into wedges.
Press each piece of fish into the flour mix to coat both sides. Set the pieces on a plate and let them rest for 8 minutes, until the coating looks damp and clings.
Heat a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium for a minute, then add the coconut oil. Lay the fish in a single layer.
Cook for 4 minutes, until the underside is crusty and golden. Flip the pieces gently and cook the other side for 4 minutes. They're done when the fish flakes easily with a fork.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the sliced onion and the lemon wedges.
method_notes: Swasthi's Fish Fry (4.99 from 184 ratings) is South Indian style: a ginger, garlic and spice rub, then a rice flour and gram flour coating rested until damp, and shallow frying in a little oil. A Little Bit of Spice (3.6 from 25) is the Kerala meen varuthathu with a straight chili, pepper and ginger-garlic paste and no flour, fried in coconut oil with curry leaves, and Maria's Menu and Suji's Cooking give the same paste. This follows the lead with rice flour only (no all-purpose flour) so it stays gluten-free, coconut oil for frying, and the rests cut to about 8 minutes each so it fits 30 minutes, which makes the coating a little lighter than a long marinade.
